title: Simple Spin(2,3)-invariant Gram quartics cannot stably align the two vector compensators

claim.statement: For two vector-5 fields in signature (2,3), neither sign of the basic Gram-determinant quartic yields a globally bounded, locally stable parallel timelike compensator vacuum.
claim.implication: Deriving the v653 rank-one alignment requires structure beyond a simple polynomial of the SO(2,3) Gram matrix.

setup.alignedPoint: V1=V2=unit vector along one timelike axis

interpretation: The second timelike direction makes the bounded Gram sign prefer an independent timelike component over parallel alignment.
The reversed sign is indefinite along spacelike/relative directions and unbounded along pairs of null vectors with growing mutual product.
The four near-zero Hessian modes are the expected common group-orbit directions, but additional negative modes invalidate the vacuum.
A positive Cartan-involution metric, constrained compensator, auxiliary field, or sequential compact-to-noncompact continuation may be needed.
falsifiers: This no-go covers the displayed renormalizable Gram-potential family, not arbitrary higher-order or constrained potentials.
Additional fields can alter the stability matrix.
A nonpolynomial domain restriction to a selected causal sheet can change global boundedness but must itself be derived.
nextBranches: Use the programme's constructed Cartan involution to define a positive alignment norm and quantify the explicit/spontaneous symmetry cost.
Test a constrained one-compensator model where the second vector copy is projected out or made massive without a VEV.
Search for sequential SO(5) alignment before analytic continuation to SO(2,3).
